agents.role: Runs the patrol loop over the watched hosts and the public vulnerability feed. It observes and records machine states; it never changes, patches, restarts, or reconfigures anything it watches.
Appends every patrol observation to the patrol record and keeps the seen-state, so the record of what was actually observed is complete and checkable afterward.

The only agent in this pack that may post across worlds. On a red patrol it runs the escalation chain to the labelled SIMULATED endpoint and sends summary counts (never hostnames) to the ops room; it never contacts a real responder, vendor, or service.

alerts.carries: The watched host label, the certificate's expiry date, and the whole days remaining. Local only; the record names the state, never a cause.
The watched host label and the certificate's expiry date, which is in the past. Local only.

The CVE id, the matched inventory entry (vendor and product as configured), and the feed's listing date. Local only; presence means the configured inventory names the product, not that an exploit was observed.
The watched host label, the port checked, and the observation time. Local only; down means the patrol's check failed, stated as an observation, never a diagnosis.
The watched host label and the sensitive port that answered without being declared expected. Local only.
The watched domain, the certificate's common name and issuer, its validity window, and the CT log entry id. Local only.
Counts only: how many red observations of each category the patrol recorded, and the patrol timestamp. Never hostnames, addresses, certificate details, or vulnerability detail.
The watched host label, the negotiated protocol version and cipher suite, the stated baseline minimum, and the drift reason. Local only.

sends.carries: Red observation counts by category and the patrol timestamp. Counts only.
never_carries: hostnames or IP addresses of watched machines

parts.proven: Pinning tests on injected signals (tests/custos/): certificate tier boundaries, feed matching against the configured inventory, exposure classification, yellow records produce zero escalation calls, red records escalate only to the labelled SIMULATED endpoint, records append and feed entries are not re-alerted across patrols; CT watcher pins: a new cert for a watched domain becomes a yellow certificate-issued record, ct_since bounds a first patrol, seen cert ids are never re-recorded; a failed certificate probe or an unparseable certificate date is an error in the summary, never data and never a patrol crash. One live stage-1 patrol against the real CISA feed (1,766 entries seen; the example inventory matched 5) is committed under worlds/custos/runs/ — a feed patrol only: the development machine has no direct network path to watched hosts, so host probes are pinned on injected signals, not live ones. UNPROVEN, stated plainly: not yet run on a booted Meta OS image, not wired as a systemd unit, never run inside a real operations room, host probes never yet run live. Live CT evidence: runs/patrol-002.jsonl holds 12 real May-2019 issuances for letsencrypt.org from crt.sh (the public query for that domain caps at 2019; two earlier attempts failed honestly with timeout/proxy errors and were retried, not fabricated). TLS grader pins (tests/custos/test_tls.py): a negotiated version below the baseline minimum is a yellow tls configuration drift record, a cipher matching a forbidden substring is drift whatever the version, a posture meeting the baseline is a baseline normal record carrying the version and cipher graded, an unrecognized version grades as drift with its reason stated, and a failed TLS probe is a summary error, never data. Live TLS postures are NOT claimed: a raw handshake from the development machine dies in the middlebox, so the grader is pinned on injected postures only.
parts.what: The patrol loop: reads the CISA known-exploited-vulnerabilities feed, checks each watched host's TLS certificate expiry, service liveness, and undeclared sensitive-port exposure, and polls Certificate Transparency logs for newly issued certs on watched domains; classifies every observation into the pack's eight categories; appends one record per observation; yellow observations stop at record + flag, red observations run the escalation chain to a labelled SIMULATED endpoint only. Pure classification core plus CLI, no model calls, no changes to watched machines. It also grades each watched host's negotiated TLS version and cipher suite against the stated baseline; drift is a yellow record, a meeting posture is recorded as baseline normal with the version and cipher it was graded on.

parts.proven: Driver pinning tests (tests/custos/test_driver.py): the STOP file halts before anything runs, a live lock blocks and a stale lock is stolen, a missing config is a logged no-op that never calls the patrol, a configured run invokes the patrol with the records and seen-state paths under the state dir, a patrol failure propagates its exit code. UNPROVEN, stated plainly: not yet run on a booted Meta OS image; the timer has never fired on real hardware.
parts.what: The standing service wiring (stage 2): the metaos-custos driver (kill switch, lock, config check, state layout) plus metaos-custos.service and metaos-custos.timer, installed by both image builds to /usr/local/bin with state at /var/lib/metaos/custos, the timer under relay.target, and the watched-host config read from /etc/metaos/custos.json.

summary: Night watch for machines: a patrol loop over real public signals (the CISA known-exploited-vulnerabilities feed, TLS certificate expiry, service liveness, undeclared sensitive-port exposure) that classifies what it actually observes into eight machine-state categories and appends every observation to a patrol record. PARTIAL: the patrol loop runtime is built and pinning-tested, one live stage-1 feed patrol is committed under runs/, and stage 2 wires the patrol as a standing Meta OS service (driver, systemd timer, state root); it has not yet run on a booted Meta OS image and nothing here runs a real operations room. The TLS grader records each watched host's negotiated protocol version and cipher suite against the stated baseline; drift is a yellow record.
summary_note: Observation aid only: it watches, classifies, and records. It never patches, restarts, reconfigures, or scans a host it was not given; it never invents an observation, and an escalation in stage 1 goes only to a labelled simulated endpoint, never to a real responder.

urgency.meaning: Red machine states: expired certificates, known-exploited vulnerabilities matching the inventory, services down, and their escalation summaries.
Yellow machine states: certificates expiring inside the warning window, anomalous exposure of undeclared sensitive ports. TLS configuration drift from the stated baseline.
Patrol completion summaries and baseline counts.

watchers.watches: Known-exploited vulnerabilities: which entries in the public feed name a vendor and product the installation's configured inventory declares. A match means the inventory names the product; it is an exposure record, not a claim that an exploit happened.

inputs: TLS handshake with each watched host
cert warning window from firstboot config
watchers.watches: Certificate expiry state per watched host: days remaining on the certificate the host actually presents, classified as baseline normal, expiring inside the warning window, or expired.

inputs: watched host list from firstboot config
watchers.watches: Service liveness and exposure: whether each watched host's service port answers, and whether any sensitive port answers that the installation did not declare expected for that host.

inputs: watched domains and ct_since from config
watchers.watches: Newly issued certificates for watched domains: a cert id not yet in the seen-state becomes a certificate-issued record (yellow). ct_since bounds a first patrol so a domain with years of history does not flood the record.
The patrol record: every observation the patrol made, its category and tier, and what the escalation chain did, kept in order as the checkable record of the watch.

inputs: TLS handshake with each watched host
watchers.watches: TLS configuration posture per watched host: the protocol version and cipher suite the host actually negotiated, graded against the installation's stated baseline; drift from the baseline is a yellow record, never an escalation.
